summary: Iteration 4 backend testing for PitchPro multi-tenant role split (platform_admin / academy_admin) + academy scoping. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4.py with 29 pytest cases — ALL 29 PASSED after applying ONE seed bug fix. Covered: role+accent on login for all 4 admin accounts, lanes/coaches/games scoping (Crease 5/3/2, Boundary & Stumps 0), admin/staff/announcements/fees/bookings/sessions/progress scoping, cross-academy validation (parent booking Boundary lane → 403, session with Boundary coach → 403, Boundary admin progress/fees for Crease user → 403), role-gating (parent → 403 on /admin/*, /staff/*; academy_admin → 403 on POST /api/academies), academy_admin CRUD (lane/coach/game tagged with own academy_id; cross-academy DELETE returns 404), announcement & game notify scope (Boundary announcement does NOT reach Crease parent), and parent booking regression. CRITICAL BUG FIXED in-place: seed_academies() had an early-return when academies already existed, so the academy_id backfill never re-ran for seeded lanes/coaches/games/bookings/sessions whose docs had academy_id=null (not missing). Effect: Crease academy_admin saw ZERO lanes/coaches/games. Applied a migration fix to ensure backfill runs every startup against docs where academy_id is missing OR null.

critical.issue: FIXED. The early-return when academies collection was non-empty skipped the academy_id backfill. Pre-existing seeded lanes/coaches/games/bookings/sessions/fees/announcements had academy_id=null (likely from a Pydantic-model-based serialization earlier), so the original backfill filter '{academy_id: {$exists: False}}' never matched them. Result: Crease academy_admin and parent (both academy=Crease) saw EMPTY lane/coach/game lists; admin/stats all showed 0; regression booking flow failed. Fixed by (a) removing early-return, (b) changing filter to '{$or:[{academy_id:{$exists:False}},{academy_id:null}]}', (c) running the same backfill for users and all 8 domain collections on every startup. Verified end-to-end: Crease now returns 5 lanes / 3 coaches / 2 games; Boundary/Stumps still 0.

minor.issue: lanes_count/coaches_count per academy appears inflated. Each academy currently reports lanes_count=5, coaches_count=3 even though only Crease actually has lanes/coaches. This is because the count includes legacy docs OR is computed without academy_id filter. Low impact (frontend-only display), but misleading.

target_date is required query param — 422 is raised BEFORE role check. So a parent (no role permission) gets 422 if target_date missing and 403 if present. Minor FastAPI ordering quirk. Consider making target_date optional (default = today) so role gating errors are returned consistently.

When platform_admin creates a lane, the new lane inherits platform_admin's academy_id (currently Crease). Platform admin should either be forced to pass academy_id explicitly OR create the lane with a null academy_id. Otherwise platform_admin can only create Crease lanes implicitly.

When Boundary academy_admin posts an announcement to audience=all, recipients count currently includes only Boundary users (correct) but there are currently 0 parents in Boundary so count=0 except for the admin themselves — worth verifying when more users are seeded in Boundary.
Still filters by user['coach_id'] which is never set on coach seed user — coach always sees empty list. Untested here but will still break coach dashboard.
still returns 200 when fee_id does not exist — inconsistent.

POST endpoints (lanes/coaches/games/fees/progress) correctly tag academy_id from target user/lane/coach, and reject cross-academy inserts with 403 — matches the review contract.

Announcement audience=all implicitly scopes to academy_id via user_query[academy_id] — correct, but the variable name 'audience=all' is misleading since it is really 'all within my academy'. Consider renaming to 'my_academy' or documenting in OpenAPI.
All role gating uses require_role() with a list — consistent. platform_admin is always included in admin-only routes, correct.

seed_academy_admins() uses each academy's declared email as the login address — that is also the academy's public contact email. Consider separating real contact email from login email to prevent accidental collision.
Still using @app.on_event (carryover iter-1) — migrate to lifespan.
Password 'AcaAdmin@1' is identical across all 3 academy admins — fine for demo, but add a 'must change on first login' flag before production.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE of Crease seeing 0 lanes: (1) On the initial empty-DB run, seed_lanes() inserted lanes WITHOUT an academy_id field. (2) seed_academies() then inserted 3 academies and tried to backfill docs matching '{academy_id: {$exists: False}}' — this SHOULD have matched, but in this environment's DB history, the lanes collection already had academy_id set to null (probably from a Pydantic model serialization or a prior migration attempt). (3) '$exists:False' does NOT match null values, so backfill silently did nothing. (4) On every subsequent startup, seed_academies() early-returned because academies.count() > 0, so the backfill never got another chance. Result: lanes have academy_id=null forever, and the scope_filter() query '{academy_id: <crease_id>}' returns 0. FIX applied: remove early-return AND change filter to '{$or:[{academy_id:{$exists:False}},{academy_id:null}]}'. Repro: fresh deploy with intermediate writes that set academy_id=null (e.g., Pydantic model with Optional[str]=None). Mitigation: explicit migration script + CI check that no seeded collection has academy_id=null.
